summary: Genetics implicate the IL-23/Th17 axis, but direct interventional evidence contradicts IL-17 blockade as a Crohn's therapy. Randomized trials of secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) and brodalumab (anti-IL-17RA) in Crohn's disease showed no efficacy and higher rates of disease worsening than placebo, and IL-17 inhibitor labels now warn about new-onset or exacerbated IBD. Mechanistic work indicates IL-17A protects the intestinal epithelial barrier, which explains the divergence from IL-23 inhibition. Absent a differentiated mechanism, the thesis is not investable.

sections.title: Target biology & human genetics
sections.summary: Genetics implicate the IL-23/Th17 axis, but IL-23-independent IL-17A protects the intestinal epithelial barrier, so blocking IL-17A is not equivalent to blocking the pathway.

claims.text: Coding variants in IL23R (e.g. R381Q) are robustly associated with Crohn's disease risk, with the rare allele conferring protection.
Multiple Th17-pathway genes (IL23R, STAT3, JAK2, CCR6, TYK2) are among the >200 IBD susceptibility loci identified by GWAS meta-analysis.
IL-17A expression is elevated in inflamed mucosa and serum of patients with active Crohn's disease compared with controls.

IL-17A produced independently of IL-23 by gut γδ T cells regulates occludin localization and maintains intestinal epithelial barrier integrity; its neutralization worsens barrier permeability in mouse colitis models.
Given genetic implication of the Th17 axis and mucosal IL-17A overexpression, neutralizing IL-17A should reduce intestinal inflammation in Crohn's disease.

sections.title: Clinical precedent
sections.summary: Psoriasis efficacy and IL-23 success in Crohn's disease no longer support a transfer argument once direct Crohn's trial data are considered.

claims.text: IL-17A inhibition (secukinumab, ixekizumab) achieved PASI 75 in roughly 77–90% of patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in Phase 3 trials.
Selective IL-23 p19 inhibition (risankizumab) induced and maintained clinical remission in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease in Phase 3.
Efficacy of IL-17 blockade in psoriasis and of IL-23 blockade in Crohn's suggests IL-17 blockade is likely to translate to Crohn's disease.

sections.title: Direct evidence: IL-17 blockade in Crohn's disease
sections.summary: Randomized trials of a ligand- and a receptor-targeting agent both failed in Crohn's disease and worsened disease in some patients, and class labels now warn about IBD. This points to a class effect.

claims.text: In a randomized, placebo-controlled proof-of-concept trial (n=59), secukinumab was ineffective in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease and was associated with more adverse events and more patients with worsening disease than placebo.
A Phase 2 trial of brodalumab (anti-IL-17RA) in Crohn's disease was terminated early after disproportionate worsening of Crohn's disease in active arms, with no evidence of efficacy.
Approved IL-17 inhibitor labels carry a warning for new-onset or exacerbated inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn's disease.

Failure with two distinct agents (ligand- and receptor-targeting) indicates a class effect of IL-17 pathway blockade in Crohn's disease, not a molecule-specific liability; a new anti-IL-17 antibody is unlikely to behave differently.

sections.title: Market & positioning
sections.summary: Unmet need persists, but class failures, label warnings and approved IL-23 inhibitors leave no credible position for an IL-17 antibody in Crohn's disease.

claims.text: A substantial share of Crohn's patients lose response to or are refractory to anti-TNF and other advanced therapies, sustaining demand for new mechanisms.

A subcutaneous IL-17 antibody has no credible positioning in Crohn's disease: prior class failures and label warnings would make regulators, investigators and prescribers resistant, while IL-23 inhibitors already address the pathway.

risks.title: Psoriasis-to-Crohn's translation risk
risks.description: Translation has already failed in randomized trials: IL-17 blockade did not work in Crohn's disease and worsened it in some patients, despite strong psoriasis efficacy.

risks.title: Patient harm / disease exacerbation
risks.description: Neutralizing IL-17A may compromise epithelial barrier integrity, consistent with observed flares in trials and label warnings. Expect heightened regulatory scrutiny and restrictive stopping rules.

risks.title: Competitive pressure from IL-23 inhibitors
risks.description: IL-23 inhibitors capture the genetically validated part of the Th17 axis without blocking barrier-protective, IL-23-independent IL-17A, which leaves no differentiated room for an IL-17 agent.

risks.title: Unvalidated enrichment biomarker
risks.description: Mucosal IL17A expression as a selection biomarker has no prospective validation; assay logistics in endoscopic biopsies may slow enrolment.

unknowns: Whether any IL-17 isoform-selective approach (e.g. IL-17F-only) avoids the barrier liability.
Whether a narrowly defined Crohn's subpopulation benefits from IL-17 blockade; no post-hoc responder signal has been published.
Dose required for adequate gut tissue exposure vs. skin.
Freedom-to-operate around existing anti-IL-17A antibody patents.

diligence_questions.question: How does the sponsor explain the secukinumab and brodalumab Crohn's results, and what data shows their antibody avoids the same outcome?
diligence_questions.rationale: Two class failures set the default expectation; the case depends on a concrete, data-backed reason this antibody would behave differently.

diligence_questions.question: Would gastroenterology KOLs and IRBs support enrolling Crohn's patients in an IL-17 trial given the label warnings?
diligence_questions.rationale: Label warnings may make sites and IRBs unwilling to enrol, which would stall the program even if the science were sound.

diligence_questions.question: Do patient-level data from prior IL-17 Crohn's trials show any subgroup with benefit (e.g. by location, prior anti-TNF exposure)?
diligence_questions.rationale: A responder subgroup is the only plausible path to a Crohn's indication given the overall negative trials.

diligence_questions.question: In human intestinal organoids, does this antibody disrupt occludin localization or barrier permeability at clinically relevant exposures?
diligence_questions.rationale: Barrier disruption is the proposed mechanism of harm; an organoid assay tests it directly and cheaply before any clinical spend.

diligence_questions.question: Could the asset be repositioned to an indication where IL-17 is validated (e.g. hidradenitis suppurativa) without IP conflicts?
diligence_questions.rationale: If Crohn's disease is not viable, the asset's value depends on an indication where IL-17 blockade already works and on freedom to operate there.

capital.milestone: Preclinical de-risking only: organoid barrier-safety package and KOL/regulatory feedback before any Crohn's clinical spend
assumptions: No Phase 2 Crohn's capital is underwritten given prior class failures
Human intestinal organoid and ex vivo biopsy barrier assays at a CRO
Access to patient-level data from prior IL-17 Crohn's trials is not assumed
Repositioning to a validated IL-17 indication would require a separate underwriting run

evidence.title: A genome-wide association study identifies IL23R as an inflammatory bowel disease gene
evidence.snippet: An uncommon coding variant (rs11209026, c.1142G>A, p.Arg381Gln) in IL23R confers strong protection against Crohn's disease.

evidence.title: Host-microbe interactions have shaped the genetic architecture of inflammatory bowel disease
evidence.snippet: Meta-analysis identifies 163 IBD loci; implicated genes are enriched for IL-23/Th17 signalling including IL23R, JAK2, STAT3 and CCR6.

evidence.title: IL23R – Crohn's disease association evidence
evidence.snippet: Overall association score 0.78; dominated by GWAS associations and genetic literature.

evidence.title: IL17A – Crohn's disease association evidence
evidence.snippet: Overall association score 0.41; evidence driven mainly by literature mining and animal models, with weak direct genetic association.

evidence.title: Increased expression of interleukin 17 in inflammatory bowel disease
evidence.snippet: IL-17 transcripts and IL-17+ cells were increased in the inflamed mucosa of patients with active Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.

evidence.title: Interleukin-23-independent IL-17 production regulates intestinal epithelial permeability
evidence.snippet: γδ T cell–derived IL-17A, produced independently of IL-23, regulates occludin and protects epithelial barrier integrity; anti-IL-17 treatment exacerbated colitis-associated barrier damage.

evidence.title: Secukinumab in plaque psoriasis — results of two phase 3 trials
evidence.snippet: ERASURE and FIXTURE: PASI 75 at week 12 achieved by 75.9–81.6% with secukinumab 300 mg vs 4.5–4.9% with placebo.

evidence.title: Phase 3 trials of ixekizumab in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis
evidence.snippet: UNCOVER-1/2/3: PASI 75 at week 12 in 87–90% of patients receiving ixekizumab every 2 weeks.

evidence.title: Risankizumab as induction therapy for Crohn's disease: results from the phase 3 ADVANCE and MOTIVATE induction trials
evidence.snippet: Risankizumab achieved significantly higher rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12 versus placebo.

evidence.title: Proof of concept study of AIN457 (secukinumab) in patients with moderate to severe Crohn's disease
evidence.snippet: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study. Status: Completed. Primary endpoint: change in CDAI at week 6.

evidence.title: Secukinumab, a human anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody, for moderate to severe Crohn's disease: unexpected results of a randomised, double-blind placebo-controlled trial
evidence.snippet: The trial was stopped for futility. Secukinumab was ineffective and associated with higher rates of adverse events compared with placebo; more patients worsened on active treatment.

evidence.title: A study of AMG 827 (brodalumab) in subjects with moderate to severe Crohn's disease
evidence.snippet: Phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled dose-ranging study. Status: Terminated.

evidence.title: Brodalumab — Crohn's disease program listing
evidence.snippet: Indication: Crohn's disease. Phase: 2. Status: Active.

evidence.title: Status mismatch: brodalumab Crohn's disease program
evidence.snippet: A pipeline listing reports the brodalumab Crohn's program as active (Phase 2), while ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01150890 lists the study as Terminated. The registry record is treated as authoritative; the listing appears stale.

evidence.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 study of brodalumab in patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease
evidence.snippet: The study was terminated early due to a disproportionate number of cases of worsening Crohn's disease in the brodalumab arms; no meaningful efficacy was observed.

evidence.title: COSENTYX (secukinumab) prescribing information — Warnings and Precautions
evidence.snippet: Inflammatory Bowel Disease: cases of IBD, in some cases serious, have been reported. Exercise caution when prescribing to patients with IBD and monitor for onset or exacerbation.

evidence.title: Overview of Crohn's disease
evidence.snippet: Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory condition of the GI tract; many patients cycle through multiple therapies over the course of disease.
